summary: Most round-1 findings are fixed. The bearing bore now clears the inner races, the FEA loads are real couples with the right resultants, the turntable is held at the bearing lands, the yoke and web fillets are in, grip is 0-65 deg, the gear sits 1.2 mm above the tower, and the accepted items (tapped servo screws, pivot wear, backlash, IK offset) are written up with reasons. The eval acceptance passes. It still fails on one blocker and one major. The four yaw-horn screw heads stand 3 mm proud of the yaw gear, and the turntable platform passes 0.5 mm above that gear once |yaw| is more than about 15 deg, so the arm cannot reach +/-90; the sweep misses this because screw heads are not modelled. The new cable route is a free loop tied to the gear guard. That tie point is inside the platform's swept area, the guard top makes a 0.5 mm shear gap with the platform, and the gear mesh is still open from both sides.

findings.issue: The yaw horn screws (yaw_horn group, 4 x M3x10, plain clearance holes) seat ON the yaw gear's top face at z 62.3 (report fasteners 'at' z 62.3, dir -Z), so the socket heads reach z 65.3. The turntable platform underside is z_plat0 = 62.8, only 0.5 mm above the gear top. At base_yaw = 0 the platform ends at x = -35 and misses the heads at x -40..-50, but it turns with the arm. I checked the yaw angles with the coupled yaw_drive rotation (-2/3) and the platform outline (x -35..15, y +/-58.7 in the turntable frame). It covers at least one screw head from |base_yaw| = 15 deg onward and covers the gear centre (-45, 0) from about 39 deg. The platform will hit the screw heads, so the arm can only turn about +/-15 deg instead of +/-90. The base_yaw sweep reports clear only because fastener heads are not solids in the sweep. This was already true in round 1 and I missed it then.
findings.fix: Counterbore the 4 horn screws into the yaw gear: iface.horn_mount(..., kind='counterbore') or bolt_pattern counterbore_depth >= head_h + 0.3 = 3.3 mm. That leaves 4.7 mm of gear under the head, and a shorter screw (M3x6 or M3x8, checked against the horn's thread depth and the spline) brings the head top below the gear face. The other option is to raise z_plat0 to >= 66.3 (gear top + 3 mm head + 1 mm), which still clears z_sh = 100. Keep >= 0.5 mm (ENGINEERING.md section 8) between the platform and anything on the rotating gear. Engine (general): add proud screw heads (male clearance sites: head_d x head_h on the seat face) as solids in the interference and sweep checks, so the next project cannot hide the same collision.

findings.issue: The cable path (round-1 major) is only partly fixed. (1) The service-loop anchor (tie slots on the guard's -Y side at about (-45, -30.3, 43.3)) is 54 mm from the yaw axis, inside the 68 mm radius the platform corners sweep. For base_yaw > about +40 deg the platform passes directly over the anchor and over the -Y guard arc. (2) The guard top is z_plat0 - 0.5 = 62.3, so the platform edge sweeps 0.5 mm over the guard's top edge. That makes a scissor at exactly the spot where the tied lead has to rise. (3) The guard is cut away for x > -25 (Rectangle 80 x 80 at -yaw_c + 60). Between each guard end and the turntable gear there is a window about 15-20 mm wide in the z 54-62 band, on both the +Y and -Y sides, that leads straight into the mesh nip. With +/-90 deg yaw each side is the in-running side at some point, and the -Y window is about 20 mm from the anchor. (4) No path is declared or checked: there is no keep-out and no channel_clear for the loop (ENGINEERING.md sections 10 and 11), and the loop runs from the +Y yoke_r back to an anchor on -Y, so it has to cross the base with nothing to guide it.
findings.fix: Put the loop anchor outside the platform's swept circle (r > 72 mm), for example tie slots on the rear clamp pad near x = -90. Take the leads from the back of yoke_r straight down outboard to that point. Close the mesh sides: extend each guard arc to meet the tower (or add a cover from the guard ends to the tower) so only the tooth passage stays open. Either keep the guard top at least 3 mm below the platform with the anchor out of the swept zone, or keep the 0.5 mm gap only where no cable can reach. Declare the loop as a keep-out or channel (about 6 mm for 3-4 leads) from the yoke_r tie slots to the anchor and check it at base_yaw -90/0/+90.

findings.issue: yoke_r_fea: the hot spot in fea_yoke_r_fea.png is at the base of the cheek's inner face near the front foot screw and the foot's front end (x about 10-15, z about 71). That is where the cheek, which runs on to x = 44 past the foot's end at x = 14, cantilevers off the bolted foot. It is not 'at a tab-screw hole edge, where the load is applied' as DESIGN.md says (the tab screws are at z 95/105). The peak there is 17.5 MPa against the 13 MPa z-allowable, and the deflection is 0.494 mm against a 0.5 mm limit. It passes on p99.9 = 7.0 MPa, and most of that stress is in the cheek plane (along layers), but the margin is thin and the explanation is wrong.
findings.fix: Extend the foot (or add a third gusset) to the front end of the cheek with a 4th M3 into the platform, or at least fillet the vertical corner where the foot ends against the cheek (r >= 2). Correct the yoke_r_fea row in DESIGN.md.

findings.issue: turntable_fea is now a sound load case (pure couples, held at the bearing lands, render matches report). Two remaining gaps. The applied moment is 1.55 N*m, not the 1.7 N*m in the 'why' text, because the 12.8 N weight is put on the foot-screw centroid at x = -11 (behind the axis) while the real arm CG is ahead of it. Both the collar face and the bearing lands are held in both directions, so the collar face can pull, which the real joint cannot do beyond the retainer preload. The retainer M3 preload also puts the printed 12 mm spindle in tension across layers, and nothing limits how tight it is made. FEA peak 9.4 MPa at the step against 13 MPa leaves room, so this is not a fail.
findings.fix: Put the 12.8 N at the arm's real CG x (or raise the couple so the net My is 1.7 N*m). In DESIGN.md assembly step 3 say: tighten the retainer screw only snug (about 0.3 N*m), enough to remove axial play, no preload.

findings.issue: The fixed-jaw post still meets the palm at a sharp inside corner (part_gripper sheet). Round 1 asked for a fillet of at least 2 mm there, and ENGINEERING.md section 5 asks for at least 1 mm on a load path. This is the across-layer critical section of gripper_fea (peak 9.9 MPa). load_axis is still not declared on gripper, finger, turntable or base (section 4: every structural part).
findings.fix: Add a 2 mm fillet at the post-to-palm and post-to-jaw inside corners. Declare load_axis on gripper, finger, turntable and base.

findings.issue: Desk mounting order: the front M4 holes at (30, +/-40) sit under the upper-arm plates at home, and DESIGN.md step 8 bolts the base down after the arm is built (step 7). Round 1 asked for this to be documented. The IK offset note was added, but the desk-screw note was not.
findings.fix: Move 'bolt/clamp the base to the desk' before step 3, or add 'swing the arm to yaw +/-90 to reach the front holes' to step 8.

findings.issue: The pivot-wear risk is accepted in DESIGN.md with a bearing-pressure estimate, which is fine. But the BOM still lists a generic 'M3 x 14 mm socket head screw (pivot)', so the buyer will get fully threaded screws.
findings.fix: In bom_extra / the pin spec, call for partially threaded M3x14 (DIN 912 with a plain shank of at least 8 mm) or ISO 7379 shoulder screws for the three pivots.
